draft.title: Public relations
card: Public relations (PR) is how a business manages the way the public sees it. The public includes customers, the local community, the media and other groups.

activity a business sets up ahead of time to build goodwill, which is the public's positive feeling toward it. Examples are sponsoring a local netball club or sending a media release about a new product.
the response when something goes wrong, such as a product fault or a social media complaint going viral. The aim is to limit damage to the business's reputation.
Crisis PR works best when the business acts quickly and tells the truth. Staying silent or hiding the problem can make the damage worse.
draft.remember: PR manages public opinion. Plan it ahead to build goodwill, or respond fast to limit damage.

a.q: Which of these is an example of crisis PR?
opts: A bakery apologises and recalls rolls that have a fault
A bakery sponsors the local primary school's fun run
A bakery sends a media release about its new sourdough
A bakery hosts an open day so locals can see how it works
a.why: A recall and apology respond to a problem that has already happened, and aim to limit damage to the bakery's reputation. The sponsorship is tempting, but it is planned in advance to build goodwill.
a.clue: Which one responds to something that has already gone wrong?

b.q: Priya owns a gym in Ballarat. A video of a member slipping on a wet floor is shared widely online. Priya posts a quick apology and explains how she will fix the problem. What is she doing?
opts: Using crisis PR to limit damage to the gym's reputation
Using planned PR to build goodwill before any problem
Using crisis PR to stop the video from being shared
Using planned PR to attract new members to the gym
b.why: The video is a problem that has already happened, so Priya is responding with crisis PR. Her aim is to limit damage to the gym's reputation. Planned PR is set up ahead of time, before anything goes wrong.
b.clue: Did Priya set this up ahead of time, or react to a problem?

a.best: A bakery apologises and recalls rolls that have a fault

b.best: Using crisis PR to limit damage to the gym's reputation
